width=\"320\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: center;\"\u003EOriginal hand painted production animation cels of Bilbo, Thorin, Balin, Bard, and Eleven Men of Lake-town from \"The Hobbit,\" 1977; Rankin\/Bass Productions; Set on a key original hand painted master production background; Size - Fifteen Characters: 6 1\/2 x 10 1\/4\", Image 8 x 10 1\/2\", Background 8 x 10 1\/2\"; Unframed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/www.untitledartgallery.com\/\" target=\"_blank\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: large;\"\u003ETo purchase this cel or to visit the Art Gallery, CLICK HERE!\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003ERankin\/Bass Productions occupies a special place in the history of American animation. Founded by Arthur Rankin Jr. and Jules Bass in the early 1960s, the studio became famous for its highly distinctive television specials, especially its beloved holiday classics such as Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer and Frosty the Snowman. Their productions were known for memorable music, richly stylized character designs, and a warm storybook quality that made them instantly recognizable. While many people primarily associate the studio with Christmas programming, Rankin\/Bass also made important contributions to fantasy animation, most notably through their adaptations of J.R.R. Tolkien’s works.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003EThe Hobbit (1977) is perhaps one of Rankin\/Bass’s most admired fantasy films. Produced as an animated television special, it adapted Tolkien’s 1937 novel into a concise yet remarkably faithful 78-minute film. The story follows Bilbo Baggins, Gandalf, Thorin Oakenshield, and the company of dwarves on their quest to reclaim the Lonely Mountain from Smaug. What makes this version so memorable is its visual atmosphere: watercolor-like backgrounds, expressive character designs, and creatures that feel both whimsical and unsettling. The animation itself was produced by Topcraft in Japan, giving the film an “anime-influenced” visual richness far beyond many American TV productions of its era.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003EMusically, The Hobbit is also deeply associated with the Rankin\/Bass style. Songs such as “The Greatest Adventure” and the haunting goblin songs help drive the narrative in a way that feels very much in line with the studio’s holiday specials. Rather than simply retelling the plot, the music reinforces the mythic and fairy-tale tone of Tolkien’s world. The voice cast is equally notable, with Orson Bean as Bilbo and John Huston as Gandalf lending the film a sense of gravitas and warmth. For many viewers, this version was their first introduction to Middle-earth long before Peter Jackson’s live-action films.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003EThree years later, Rankin\/Bass returned to Tolkien with The Return of the King (1980), an animated television film that served as a sequel to The Hobbit. Unlike Peter Jackson’s later trilogy, this film adapts only the final volume of The Lord of the Rings, omitting the events of The Fellowship of the Ring and The Two Towers except for a brief recap at the beginning. This gives the film a compressed and somewhat episodic structure, moving quickly through Frodo and Sam’s journey to Mount Doom and the climactic destruction of the Ring.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003EAlthough The Return of the King is often viewed as less successful than The Hobbit, it remains fascinating as part of Rankin\/Bass’s Tolkien legacy. The film retains the studio’s signature musical storytelling and visual style, with memorable sequences such as the orc marching song “Where There’s a Whip, There’s a Way.” Its framing device, with Bilbo hearing the tale retold in Rivendell, gives it an almost ballad-like structure. While critics and even Arthur Rankin himself later regarded it as less effective, the film has nonetheless earned a nostalgic following among fans of classic animation and Tolkien adaptations.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003ETogether, these two films demonstrate how Rankin\/Bass could move beyond holiday nostalgia and successfully bring epic fantasy to television audiences. Their adaptations remain important not only as Tolkien films but as landmarks in animation history, bridging American storytelling sensibilities with Japanese artistry through Topcraft’s work. For many fans, they represent a uniquely dreamlike and folkloric vision of Middle-earth that still holds charm nearly fifty years later.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003EThe Hobbit (1977) is a landmark animated adaptation of J.R.R. Tolkien’s beloved fantasy novel, produced by Rankin-Bass and animated by the Japanese studio Topcraft. The film introduced generations of viewers to Middle-earth through its distinctive visual style, memorable songs, and faithful presentation of the novel’s central themes of adventure, friendship, and the corrupting influence of greed. Topcraft’s contribution to the production is especially significant in animation history, as the studio would later evolve into companies that included Pacific Animation and the future Studio Ghibli. The film’s richly painted backgrounds, credited to Hidetoshi Kaneko and Minoru Nishida, helped create a vivid and atmospheric version of Tolkien’s world despite the constraints of television animation.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003EThe original hand painted production animation cel setup captures a pivotal moment in the story at approximately the 50:12 mark of the film. In this scene, Bard and Thorin Oakenshield forge an alliance in Esgaroth, better known as Lake-Town. Thorin declares, “What help we can offer will be yours, and we trust to your gratitude when the dragon Smaug is killed and your kingdom is regained!” The statement reflects the mutual interests of the dwarves and the people of Lake-Town, both of whom hope to benefit from the defeat of Smaug and the restoration of prosperity to the region. This alliance serves as an important narrative step toward the climactic events surrounding the Lonely Mountain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003EThe image itself provides an excellent example of the artistry involved in traditional cel animation. In the foreground, Bard stands prominently on the left side of the composition, addressing Thorin and the dwarves. His confident posture and raised arm emphasize his leadership role among the people of Lake-Town. Opposite him stand Thorin and members of his company, including the figure of Bilbo Baggins visible between the dwarves. The arrangement of the characters visually reinforces the diplomatic nature of the scene, with the two groups facing one another as they negotiate their shared future. The gathered townspeople in the background further suggest that this is a public and significant occasion.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003EParticularly striking is the original Key Master background, painted in gouache on board. The artwork depicts the wooden walkways and buildings of Lake-Town stretching into the distance beneath a softly colored sky. The architecture creates depth and perspective, drawing the viewer’s eye through the settlement toward the horizon. The background also includes the Lonely Mountain looming beyond the town, a constant reminder of the dwarves’ ultimate destination and the dragon Smaug’s presence. The careful rendering of the environment demonstrates the skill of the background artists and contributes greatly to the film’s immersive fantasy atmosphere.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003EAs a piece of animation history, this setup is especially noteworthy because it consists of four original hand-painted cels displayed over their original production background. Such complete setups are considerably rarer than individual cels, as animation elements were often separated or discarded after filming. The artwork preserves a key dramatic moment from one of the most celebrated animated fantasy films of the twentieth century. Beyond its value as a collectible, the cel offers insight into the craftsmanship behind The Hobbit and serves as a tangible connection to a production that helped shape the visual legacy of Tolkien’s work on screen.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"font_7\" style=\"text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E#RankinBass #RankinBassProductions #ArthurRankinJr #JulesBass #ClassicAnimation Its acclaimed voice cast included\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EJodi Benson\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EChristopher Daniel Barnes\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EPat Carroll\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ESamuel E. Wright\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EJason Marin\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EKenneth Mars\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EBuddy Hackett\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, and\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ERené Auberjonois\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"2322\" data-start=\"1193\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Ci data-end=\"1213\" data-start=\"1193\"\u003EThe Little Mermaid\u003C\/i\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Ealso holds an important place in animation history as the final Disney feature film to use traditional hand-painted animation cels. During development, Clements and Musker expanded the role of the story’s villain, Ursula, transforming her into one of Disney’s most iconic antagonists. The role went through several casting possibilities before its unforgettable final form emerged. Actress\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EBeatrice Arthur\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Ewas initially considered for the part but declined the role. Veteran stage actress\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EElaine Stritch\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Elater accepted it, though creative disagreements over the musical style ultimately led to her departure. The role was then given to\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EPat Carroll\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, whose theatrical and larger-than-life performance became legendary. Carroll famously described Ursula as “part Shakespearean actress, with all the flair, flamboyance and theatricality, and part used-car salesman with a touch of con artist.” Her commanding voice and wicked charisma defined the character and helped make Ursula one of the most memorable villains in Disney history.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"3034\" data-start=\"2324\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EThe animation of Ursula was originally intended for legendary Disney animator\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EGlen Keane\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E. However, after hearing Jodi Benson perform “Part of Your World,” Keane became determined to animate Ariel instead. Ursula was ultimately assigned to Disney animator\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ERuben Aquino\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, who later described her as his favorite character he had ever animated. Aquino explained that he drew inspiration from Pat Carroll’s vocal performance, the story sketches, and extensive research into octopus movement to make Ursula’s motions feel fluid and convincing. He noted that Carroll’s extraordinary performance made the scenes feel as though they “almost animate themselves.”\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"3900\" data-start=\"3036\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EAccompanying Ursula are her sinister henchmen, Flotsam and Jetsam, a pair of eerie green moray eels who slither constantly at her side. Their unusual eyes are especially striking: one eel has a yellow left eye and white right eye, while the other’s colors are reversed. Their names come from the nautical phrase “flotsam and jetsam,” meaning discarded or useless debris. The pair often speak in unison, finish one another’s sentences, and weave their bodies together in hypnotic motions. They also possess a magical ability to merge their glowing white eyes into a crystal-ball-like portal that allows Ursula to spy on the outside world from within her cavern. Both characters were voiced by\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EPaddi Edwards\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, who also voiced Lucy the goose in\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003E101 Dalmatians: The Series\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Eand Atropos in\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EHercules\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"4322\" data-start=\"3902\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EThis remarkable animation cel setup comes from Ursula’s unforgettable musical number,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EPoor Unfortunate Souls\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, widely regarded as one of the highlights of the film. The scene features Ursula leaning dramatically toward Flotsam and Jetsam, who appear in full figure with their eyes glowing open as they listen to her scheme. At this moment, Ursula begins singing the opening lines of her signature song:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: justify;\"\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cblockquote data-end=\"4434\" data-start=\"4324\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"4434\" data-start=\"4326\"\u003E“I admit that in the past I’ve been a nasty,\u003Cbr data-end=\"4373\" data-start=\"4370\" \/\u003EThey weren’t kidding when they called me, well, a witch.”\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/blockquote\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"4669\" data-is-last-node=\"\" data-is-only-node=\"\" data-start=\"4436\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EThe sequence perfectly captures the theatrical charm, menace, and dark humor that made Ursula such an unforgettable Disney villain, while also showcasing the extraordinary artistry of Disney’s final era of hand-painted cel animation. A fantastic addition to any animation art collection!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: center;\"\u003E\n\u003Ca class=\"ot-hashtag aaTEdf\" text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EReleased in 1989,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EThe Little Mermaid\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Emarked a triumphant return to musical storytelling for Disney animation and became the 28th film in the Walt Disney Animated Classics series. Produced by\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ca class=\"decorated-link cursor-pointer\" data-end=\"306\" data-start=\"210\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_new\"\u003EWalt Disney Pictures\u003Cspan aria-hidden=\"true\" class=\"ms-0.5 inline-block align-middle leading-none\"\u003E\u003Csvg aria-hidden=\"true\" class=\"block h-[0.75em] w-[0.75em] stroke-current stroke-[0.75]\" data-rtl-flip=\"\" height=\"20\" width=\"20\" xmlns=\"http:\/\/www.w3.org\/2000\/svg\"\u003E\u003Cuse fill=\"currentColor\"\u003E\u003C\/use\u003E\u003C\/svg\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Eand animated by Walt Disney Feature Animation, the film premiered in theaters on November 17, 1989. Inspired by the classic Danish fairy tale by\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EHans Christian Andersen\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, the story follows Ariel, a spirited young mermaid princess who dreams of leaving the sea behind to become human.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"1279\" data-start=\"607\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EThe film was written, directed, and produced by\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ERon Clements\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Eand\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EJohn Musker\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, with a celebrated musical score by\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EAlan Menken\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Eand lyrics by\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EHoward Ashman\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E. Its talented voice cast included\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EJodi Benson\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Eas Ariel,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EChristopher Daniel Barnes\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003Eas Prince Eric,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EPat Carroll\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Eas Ursula,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ESamuel E. Wright\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Eas Sebastian, alongside\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EJason Marin\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EKenneth Mars\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EBuddy Hackett\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, and\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ERené Auberjonois\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"2128\" data-start=\"1281\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EDisney devoted more money and resources to\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ci data-end=\"1344\" data-start=\"1324\"\u003EThe Little Mermaid\u003C\/i\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Ethan it had to any animated feature in decades. In addition to its primary animation studio in Glendale, California, Disney opened a new satellite animation facility at the Disney-MGM Studios theme park in Lake Buena Vista, Florida. The Florida studio’s earliest work included producing the Roger Rabbit short\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ci data-end=\"1678\" data-start=\"1655\"\u003ERoller Coaster Rabbit\u003C\/i\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Eand providing ink-and-paint support for\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ci data-end=\"1739\" data-start=\"1719\"\u003EThe Little Mermaid\u003C\/i\u003E. Another innovative step for Disney animation at the time was the use of live-action performers as motion-reference models for animators. Although primarily known as a Broadway performer, Jodi Benson was selected to voice Ariel, while actress and comedian\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ESherri Stoner\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Eperformed many of Ariel’s scenes in live-action reference sessions to guide the animators.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"2451\" data-start=\"2130\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EThe film also holds an important place in animation history as the last Disney feature to use traditional hand-painted animation cels. This painstaking process gave the film its rich, luminous visual style and marked the end of an era before Disney’s transition into digital ink-and-paint technology in the early 1990s.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"3131\" data-start=\"2453\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EAmong the film’s most beloved characters is Sebastian, the red Jamaican crab who serves as King Triton’s court composer and reluctant guardian to Ariel. Voiced with warmth and comic brilliance by Samuel E. Wright, Sebastian became one of Disney’s most memorable side characters. Wright improvised the famous line, “Teenagers, they think they know everything. You give them an inch, they swim all over you!” Animators\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EDuncan Marjoribanks\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ETom Sito\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, and\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EWill Finn\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003Edeveloped Sebastian’s expressive personality, drawing inspiration from legendary entertainer\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ESammy Davis Jr.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"3731\" data-start=\"3133\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003ESebastian’s signature song,\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EUnder the Sea\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E, became one of Disney’s defining musical numbers. Composed by Alan Menken with lyrics by Howard Ashman, the song was partly inspired by “The Beautiful Briny” from the 1971 Disney film\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003EBedknobs and Broomsticks\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E. Its lively Caribbean calypso sound reflected musical traditions originating in\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"whitespace-normal\"\u003ETrinidad and Tobago\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E. Performed by Samuel E. Wright, “Under the Sea” won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 1989 and later received the Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media in 1991.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"4167\" data-start=\"3733\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EWithin the story, the song serves as Sebastian’s heartfelt attempt to persuade Ariel to remain under the sea and abandon her longing to become human and live with Prince Eric. Sebastian enthusiastically praises the carefree wonders of ocean life while humorously describing the hardships of the human world. Yet despite his efforts, Ariel remains consumed by her dreams of life on land, swimming away before the song even concludes.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"4483\" data-start=\"4169\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EThe animation cel shown here comes from a memorable scene in which Ariel brushes her hair with a “dinglehopper” — a fork she believes to be a human grooming tool — while Sebastian anxiously sits nearby on a table. Frustrated and exhausted after trying to help Ariel succeed in the human world, Sebastian laments:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cblockquote data-end=\"4571\" data-start=\"4485\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"4571\" data-start=\"4487\"\u003E“This has got to be, without a doubt, the single most humiliating day of my life.”\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/blockquote\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"4895\" data-start=\"4573\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EAfter Ariel drifts off to sleep, Sebastian tenderly attempts to coach her on how to win Prince Eric’s affection, demonstrating how to bat her eyes and pucker her lips. Realizing she has fallen asleep during his instructions, he softens, blows out the candle beside her bed, curls up near her pillow, and quietly remarks:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cblockquote data-end=\"4964\" data-start=\"4897\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"4964\" data-start=\"4899\"\u003E“You are hopeless, child. You know dat? Completely hopeless...”\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/blockquote\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp data-end=\"5199\" data-is-last-node=\"\" data-is-only-node=\"\" data-start=\"4966\" style=\"-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black; font-style: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-decoration-line: none; text-decoration-style: solid; text-decoration-thickness: auto; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px;\"\u003EThe scene perfectly captures the affectionate bond between Ariel and Sebastian — a relationship filled with humor, frustration, loyalty, and genuine love — and remains one of the film’s most charming and emotionally resonant moments.\u0026nbsp;A wonderful addition to any animation art collection!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: center;\"\u003E\n\u003Ca class=\"ot-hashtag
